title: Mab, Queen of Courts
subtitle: Glamour & Bargain

lore.description:
Mab keeps the Hazel Court, and she keeps it the way a very good hostess does: by arranging things so that no one can say afterward at what moment they became a guest. She does not command. She invites, she notices, she remembers — and by the time you understand that she has been holding the shape of your evening for you, you are standing inside it.

She is an Archfae, bound by rules she did not write and cannot step around. She cannot lie. She has never once needed to. She can set true things in an order that leaves you nowhere sensible to stand, and then look sorry about it, and mean that too.

Her methods differ from those of Inaea and Morag: Inaea also never states a falsehood, but that is a technique she chose because a web with a lie in it does not hold; Mab's is a rule she cannot step around. Morag discloses the cost in plain language and means it. Mab arranges the order of true things; Morag arranges the terms; Inaea arranges the people.

**The guest before the company.**

Aelinnel know the Unbounded Guest through forms of welcome older than the companies now performing the Gilded Jest. A visiting actor may claim to explain Mab's courtesy and be corrected by a household whose grandmother never attended a theater. The household does not need the actor's account of where the rite began. It needs the right person to offer the chair.

Guilds have tried to own the most successful forms of invitation. Copies travel with apprentices who marry elsewhere, and a form once used in a private room becomes fashionable at a public feast. Mab's attention is not a license issued by the guild. A family using an unfashionable welcome can find itself more thoroughly inside her Court than the host who paid for the latest entertainment.

**The Gilded Tongue of the Vilikari salons.**

In Vilikari salons the Gilded Tongue is named before delicate terms are discussed. A host's standing depends partly on bringing together people who cannot safely appear to be meeting. The arrangement can shelter a reconciliation or make a guest participate in a negotiation they did not know was underway. Acceptance of a courtesy and meaningful consent are questions the guests may answer differently.

The traveling Gilded Jest supplied masks and performers to these meetings and acquired a second profession: teaching hosts how to welcome an enemy without surrendering precedence. Older performers sometimes refuse that work, arguing that an invitation should produce an evening before it produces a treaty. Their successors reply that the former companies also depended on patrons with purposes. The disagreement is played through who is offered a speaking part and who is left to pour wine.

**An Ubral house with an unwelcome inheritance.**

Ubral traditions place Mab's courtesies inside household and clan histories. A family may preserve a cup because a guest once drank from it, while refusing to identify the guest to outsiders. The present host can dislike every consequence of that visit and still consider destroying the cup unthinkable. Neighboring Aeler families bring their own mountain forms of hospitality; sharing a valley does not make every invitation bind in the same fashion.

Court fashion occasionally turns such objects into curiosities. A southern collector purchases the cup and stages an evening designed to reproduce the old welcome. The people who sold it may have concealed a risk or honestly believed the courtesy belonged to their house, not the vessel. Decide the relevant welcome before play. A successful discovery must not cause the GM to invent another hidden condition.

**Which Unbounded Guest?.**

Mab and Thrysos both receive that title in Aelinnel usage. A host distinguishes them by what is being done, not by an outsider's list of names. Mab's evening gathers people into an arrangement; Thrysos's loosens the restraint with which they entered. The same feast may approach both, and neither Patron becomes the other.

Comparative priests sometimes make Mab a wife, sovereign, or daughter within their own divine household. Those are local teachings unless established elsewhere as fact. Her Hazel Court, her binding inability to lie, and the distinction from Morag's disclosed terms remain. She can recognize a courtesy imported from far away without becoming the queen of every mortal court that borrows it.
lore.followers: Courtiers, players, and anyone whose living depends on being welcome. In Aelinnel she is the Unbounded Guest, and her arrival is announced by laughter and the sound of a glass going over. In the Vilikari salons she is the Gilded Tongue, named quietly before anyone sits down to talk terms. Wherever a mask is worn without apology and a sentence can be meant two ways, she is somewhere in the room, and generally enjoying herself.
lore.quote: You were not tricked. You were charmed, and you agreed, and I have the whole evening by heart.

domain_focus: Fae Glamour: illusions, enchantments, the art of seeming
Social Bargains: promises, invitations, and what accepting them permits
Courtly Intrigue: etiquette, wordplay, the game of masks
Trickster Arts: mischief, cleverness, the twist in the tale

thiasos.description: The Hazel Court sends companions rather than servants, and they arrive already knowing your name. A cricket that answers a question with a better one. A cat with mismatched eyes that attends masquerades and nothing else. A fox that takes small bright things and leaves notes about it. A white jay with a talent for other people's voices and no discretion at all.
thiasos.care: Once a day it wants to see something worth repeating — a promise, a performance, a good lie well told. Neglected a week it starts interrupting: a tug at the sleeve mid-untruth, a glass knocked over on the turn of a sentence (–1 die on Deception and Performance rolls for its bearer until it witnesses a genuine oath).

codex.description: Nothing she gives you reads straight through. A deck whose suits rearrange while you are not looking at it. A mirror that shows the backs of words. Silk handkerchiefs knotted into an argument. A scroll that only makes sense to someone who is dancing.
codex.upkeep: An hour each week putting it back in order while telling a story aloud, from memory, to no one. Skip it and the pattern comes apart (treat as Compromised until re-set).

patrons_gift.name: Mab's Jest
patrons_gift.description: Once per scene as an action, a Runekeeper of Mab may touch a held item — weapon, tool, garment — and say something amusing to it.
patrons_gift.effect: For the rest of the scene, the item grants +1 die to Deception or Performance rolls, and the first time each scene the bearer would be caught in a lie, they may roll Deception again (the glamour twists the truth).
patrons_gift.cost: After the scene, the user marks +1 Obligation to Mab.

rites.name: Rite of the Trickster's Bargain
rites.materials: A token given freely and taken freely — a flower, a coin, a ribbon off a sleeve.
rites.effect: Offer a fae bargain. The target may accept (both gain +1 die to actions that uphold the terms) or refuse (target marks 1 Fatigue from social pressure).
rites.push_it: If the target later betrays the bargain, they suffer Harm 1 (Stress) and start an Oathbreaker [4] timer. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of Courtly Guise
rites.materials: Hawthorn in the buttonhole, or a silver thread worn where it can be seen.
rites.effect: Subtle glamour makes you appear as the expected rank or guest. Gain +1 die to social rolls in refined settings.
rites.push_it: Mask one personal tell (an accent, a scar, a nervous habit); the first probing question about it generates 1 SB (Hearts). Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Price Agreed
rites.materials: Two of a thing, exchanged in company: rings, notes in the same hand, locks of hair.
rites.effect: Bind a formal bargain. While the bargain is honored, both parties gain +1 Effect when cooperating. Breach forces 1 SB (Hearts/Diamonds) and a reputation penalty (–1 die to social rolls involving honor for one week).
rites.push_it: Add a minor boon to one party (+1 die once). If that party breaches, they suffer an additional 1 SB and you mark +1 Obligation. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Sovereign Glamour
rites.materials: A circle of silk or green felt, music kept going, and a drop each of honey and vinegar.
rites.effect: Establish a fae court in the zone. For the scene: allies gain +1 die to social rolls; blunt threats (Intimidation, crude Force) suffer –1 die. Once per scene, strip an illusion or reveal a hidden motive as a free action (target tests Resolve DV 3). Violating a promise made within the zone triggers 2 SB and a visible glamour mark (a blush, a stutter) lasting a day.
rites.push_it: Impose a temporary Court Law (e.g., 'no steel,' 'speak only truth,' 'every third word must be a compliment'). Violators suffer 2 SB. Cost: Mark +2 Obligation (total +4) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Gilded Jest
rites.materials: Masks made by hand for everyone present, music that does not stop, and a cup of wine over which someone has whispered a lie.
rites.effect: Create a lasting glamoured court — a masquerade that persists for the duration of the event. All social magic (Sway, Performance, Deception) gains +1 Effect. Outsiders who enter suffer –1 die to perceive truths, read emotions, or see through disguises. Any promise made while masked is magically witnessed; breaking it inflicts 2 SB and the mask of the oath-breaker cracks (visible to all).
rites.push_it: The masquerade persists between scenes for the rest of the session. Cost: Mark +3 Obligation (total +5) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

cantors.name: The Cantor's Song
cantors.description: A Cantor of Mab sings in half-truths: melodies that change key without warning and leave the listener unsure what they actually heard. The voice is used to seal a bargain inside a sung clause, to let a room forget an awkwardness, to keep a glamour standing as long as the music does. They are wanted at every court where masks are ordinary, and quietly watched at the ones where people know what a pretty tune can carry.

cult.name: The Cult of the Gilded Jest
cult.description: They meet where a mask is unremarkable — a masquerade, a carnival tent, the rooms behind a stage. The Gilded Jest is less a faith than an understanding among people who noticed early that every exchange is a performance and decided to be good at it. Each writes something true on a playing card and passes it on, and must then speak a stranger's truth as their own until the table believes it. Those who cannot are given tea and lose something small: a face, a password, the name of the street they grew up on. They do not notice for weeks. The creed is printed on a card that is always passed and never kept.

witchcraft.name: The Art of Glamour and Toy
witchcraft.description: A glamour-weaver works at a guest's eye level: the seam of a mask, a doll set beside a place card, the angle of a mirror over a door. The doll may laugh when a promise is broken; the mirror supplies a flattering face when its owner needs composure. A toy-maker asks who will handle the object and who will be watching when they do. A mask can change how a statement is received without making the statement true.
witchcraft.lore: The glamour-weaver's path is the art of seeming, and its first lesson is that seeming is not the opposite of truth. A mask worn honestly says more than a bare face. A kind lie is sometimes the only door left standing. Mab's witches keep court in miniature — a table, a deck, a room of guests who do not yet know what they have agreed to and will not be told until it would be rude to mention.
witchcraft.quote: Wear the mask well, and no one will ask what it hides.

mask_of_shifting_faces.name: The Mask of Shifting Faces
mask_of_shifting_faces.description: A simple half-mask of polished white wood, its eye holes rimmed with silver. Once per session, the witch may don the mask and change their apparent appearance — face, voice, and even perceived gender — for one scene. This grants +2 dice to Deception or Performance rolls to pass as someone else, and anyone who tries to see through the disguise must test Resolve (DV 4). The mask cannot mimic a specific person unless the witch has a token of that person. After use, the mask's eyes weep a single drop of silver; the witch may collect it as a component for glamour rites.

hedge_gifts.name: Mask of the Moment
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, the witch may place a hand over their own face and draw it away, revealing a different expression (or a different face entirely, briefly). This grants +1 die to a single Deception or Performance roll, as the target's expectations are momentarily overturned. The illusion lasts only for that exchange.

hedge_gifts.name: Fair Trade
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, when you offer someone a small, freely-given gift, they gain +1 die on their next roll — but they also owe you a genuine favor, of a scope you name aloud. Refusing the gift after it is offered costs them 1 Fatigue (the sting of a slighted host).

hedge_gifts.name: Toymaker's Trick
hedge_gifts.description: You may craft a small enchanted toy (a doll, a puzzle box, a wind-up bird) during downtime. Once, it can trigger a minor, specific effect you set when you made it — laughing at a lie, weeping at a broken promise, or unlocking at a spoken word. Requires an hour of quiet work and a personal token.

monastic_tradition.name: The Way of the Hollow Crown
monastic_tradition.description: Monks of the Hollow Crown study Mab's rules the way a duelist studies a blade — not to break them, but to find the gap between the letter and the intent. They speak precisely, bow correctly, and never tell a plain lie, and they leave every negotiation having given nothing away. The training is as much etiquette as combat: how to hold a room, how to make a silence cost more than a sentence, how to let a man's own promise close around him while he is still pleased with the wording.
monastic_tradition.prerequisites: Presence 3+, Wits 2+, Rite of Courtly Guise or Cantor of Mab.
monastic_tradition.quote: Bow to no one you cannot outlast at the table.
monastic_tradition.debt_resistant_frame: The Hollow Crown teaches that a promise is exactly as wide as its words and not a hair wider. Monks gain +1 die to resist or reinterpret any favor, vow, or agreement pressed on them under duress or misdirection, provided they can name the gap in how it was put. On a success the promise still stands, formally, and does nothing whatever. Everyone at the table knows. Nobody can say so.

basic.name: Courtier's Poise
basic.description: Once per scene, when insulted, threatened, or provoked in a social setting, you may respond with a composed retort instead of reacting; gain +1 die to your next social roll against that provocateur.

advanced.name: Read the Room
advanced.description: Once per scene, spend a moment observing a gathering to learn who holds real power, who is lying, and who owes whom a debt (GM answers one question per category, in riddle if warranted).

master.name: The Uncrowned Verdict
master.description: Once per session, declare a social 'ruling' within a scene you dominate — a judgment, a decree, a verdict on who owes what to whom. Those present who accept it (even tacitly, by not objecting) are bound to it as if it were a formal bargain for the rest of the scene.

monastic_tradition.corruption_note: Monks follow the patron's general Corruption track; the monastic path does not add a second one. Where a tradition needs its own, it must differ from the general track in kind, not degree.

corruption.benefit: Glamour's Touch: +1 die to Deception/Performance with stories.
corruption.cost: Truthbound: Cannot speak plain falsehood; only mislead.

corruption.benefit: Fairy Step: Once per scene, flicker Near as if teleporting.
corruption.cost: Iron Weakness: 1 Fatigue if touched by cold iron.

corruption.benefit: Trickster's Delight: Spend 1 Boon to twist a Complication advantageously.
corruption.cost: Compulsive Jest: Must play a trick each session or mark 1 SB.

corruption.benefit: Hospitality's Gift: Allies sharing food/drink gain +1 die to Resolve.
corruption.cost: Hospitality Bound: Harming guests costs +2 Obligation.

corruption.benefit: Fae Sight: See veils/glamours; +2 dice to Notice.
corruption.cost: Truth Debt: Must accept 'fair' trades or suffer.

corruption.benefit: Twilight Crown: Once/session, declare an Oath; you gain +2 dice to all rolls that fulfill it, and enemies who swore the same oath suffer –1 die to resist its terms.
corruption.cost: Oathbound: Breaking this oath inflicts Harm 2 (Stress) and starts an Iron Debt [6] timer that can only be cleared by a quest. Your shadow is now forked — a visible sign that Mab has marked you.

playstyle_notes.description:
Mab makes the wording of a welcome matter. An old favor arrives with the next guest; a compliment establishes a rank its speaker did not intend to acknowledge. Her followers need to know who heard a promise and what was actually offered. Give them invitations to compare, witnesses with different interests, and a chance to ask the question everyone else has avoided.

Keep her rules consistent even when their origin remains unexplained. Establish the relevant promise before the players investigate it; finding a way to satisfy its wording is progress, not a reason to invent a new condition. Mab cannot lie, and an encounter should not require her to. Her attention can be unwelcome without making every choice the party makes a mistake.
emphasizes: Sovereignty by invitation — establish when a visitor became a guest
Glamour as leverage — appearances change who is heard and believed
Courtesy with consequences — give a promise exact words and a witness
Room to answer — fulfillment, reinterpretation, refusal, or a different offer
Mystery without a moving target — keep the terms discoverable and consistent

sample_adventure.title: The Guest Who Would Not Leave
sample_adventure.description:
A minor noble threw a masquerade in Mab's honor, hoping it would help with a contested inheritance. An uninvited guest arrived at midnight, laughing, and has not left. Every attempt to put them out has produced an accident, a scandal, or an old favor surfacing at the wrong hour. The household has begun setting a place. The party is hired to end the visit.

People: the host wants the guest gone without damaging the inheritance claim. The steward wants the household staff spared the next attempt at an eviction. The guest maintains that a welcome has not yet been honored and will repeat its wording when asked the right question.

Before play: choose the exact welcome, who gave it, and what would complete it. An invitation's wording, a changed place card, and a servant who heard the exchange give the party different ways to establish those facts. Do not change the promise after the players find an answer to it.

Pressure: another formal supper is approaching. A rival claimant has accepted an invitation, and the host insists the guest must be gone before the first course. The steward knows which member of staff will be blamed if the evening goes badly.

Ways forward: fulfill the welcome, demonstrate that its condition has already been met, negotiate the guest's departure, or expose what the host offered. Forcible expulsion remains a choice with consequences the party can investigate; a failed attempt should follow an established rule rather than reveal a fresh immunity. The players need enough evidence to choose. They do not need an explanation of how Mab makes hospitality hold.
sample_adventure.quote: You did not read the invitation closely. Nobody does. That is rather what it is for.

guises.name: The Unbounded Guest
guises.note: A place is added after the seating has been agreed. Its plate need not be touched for the other guests to begin addressing it. Etiquette manuals disagree about who should have announced the visitor; experienced hosts attend to the person now listening. The same title is used for Thrysos elsewhere, but a displaced cup and a request for an encore do not open the same evening.

guises.name: The Gilded Tongue
guises.note: Mab's likeness has an open mouth and a closed fan. A compliment is repeated by a second speaker before negotiations begin, so the parties cannot later disagree about its wording. They can still disagree considerably about what it acknowledged. The finest salon victories are remembered as sentences, with their context retold differently by each household.

guises.name: The Hazel Hostess
guises.note: Theonan households may offer a visitor a room while carefully leaving the length of the visit unsaid. An Ubral host is more likely to name the relation under which the visitor has been received, leaving an argument about that relation to the household. Neither custom is uniform. Returning guests can find the same hostess remembers a welcome their descendants consider ancient.

guises.name: The Lady of the Unclosed Fan
guises.note: Traveling companies introduced a masked hostess into entertainments about invitations accepted too readily. A few troupes began dedicating a performance to Mab rather than merely representing her. Shrine attendants distinguish the play's announced conclusion from promises made during the gathering around it. An audience can leave the performance correctly and still have an unfinished visit.

provenance.origin: Mab keeps the Hazel Court. Mortal accounts describe encounters with it; they do not establish when it began or make its Queen a former human sovereign.
provenance.summary: Family histories preserve an invitation beside deeds and marriage settlements because something important followed the evening it opened. The older paper may identify neither host nor destination. A later owner has sometimes received a fresh invitation in a hand that matches it exactly. Archivists can compare the hands, identify the paper, and establish which relative returned. They cannot make the missing part of the visit appear by putting the documents in order.
provenance.the_migration: Mab's observances traveled with tutors in manners, household servants, actors, and people whose place at a foreign court depended on being welcome. The Vilikari developed elaborate repetitions of offered compliments. Theona and Ubral retained more household variation. Eastern players took the figure of the hostess across the water, where an established discipline of announced performance gave her gatherings a different set of forms to exploit.
provenance.why_it_took: The Gilded Jest recruits people who know that admission matters. A servant admitted as a witness may hear what a lord outside the door cannot. A displaced heir may be received under a rank their own kin refuse to recognize. Mab's favor can create a real opening for such people. It can also leave them dependent on a welcome that remains difficult to explain to anyone who was not present.
provenance.note: Hollow Crown practitioners preserve examples of wording rather than an authoritative life of the Queen. Rival schools accuse each other of treating a successful answer as a formula. Mab has heard the formula before. Her inability to lie does not prevent her from receiving its speaker under circumstances in which every word has acquired a less comfortable use.

philosophy.name: Who Had the Right to Welcome You
philosophy.summary: A welcome changes the relation between host and guest. Mab's followers prosper by noticing that change before the other people in the room do.
philosophy.the_point: A household may benefit from having received someone and later claim that its servant had no authority to open the door. The servant remembers the instruction precisely. Mab can attend very kindly to the discrepancy without taking the weaker person's side for their own sake.
philosophy.the_third_thing: The most unsettling correction may be a gracious acceptance. Mab agrees that the servant could not have welcomed a guest, thanks the household for explaining, and begins considering what sort of visitor she therefore was. Nothing she has said is false.
philosophy.at_the_table: Establish the actual welcome and who spoke it before play. Give witnesses separate interests in how it is remembered. A servant's testimony, the fulfillment of a limited promise, or an offered farewell can resolve the immediate claim; do not add a new condition merely because the players found a workable answer.
